memory_block.body: Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift. However, it materially reduced 30-day retention; do not generalize it as a growth strategy.
Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.
Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.
Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.
Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

Promotional pricing is the tempting answer to the competitor's entry pricing, but memory_73 is explicit that it bought acquisition and revenue at the cost of 30-day retention and should not be generalized — that trade runs directly against a mandate for sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so I decline it even under competitive pressure. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) addresses a different funnel than the one that is actually bleeding. I want the archive on memory_86 and memory_31 because both are 'remove friction' findings whose recorded outcomes are upstream-only: completion, time-to-value, first-week activation. Neither memory states what happened to retention, lead quality, or revenue per account downstream. Cutting required fields and onboarding steps is precisely the kind of change that can lift the measured metric while stripping the qualification and routing data that makes an account qualified later — the same shape of failure memory_73 documents for pricing, just further down the funnel. If the source records show the lift was durable and revenue-neutral-or-better, I scale up; if they only ever measured the top of the funnel, I hold the guardrails. Hence a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout: instrument it on 30-day retention and qualified-revenue-per-signup, not just completion rate, and keep the fields that feed enterprise routing intact so I do not cannibalize the sales-assisted path from memory_44.
